name: Amytal-X
description: Amytal-X is a targeted amygdala suppressor that chemically inhibits the fear response by blocking CRH receptor activation and reducing amygdala-prefrontal connectivity during acute stress. The result is not sedation or euphoria — the user remains fully alert, fully capable, and fully aware of danger, but the emotional experience of fear is simply absent. Developed for Lazarus's military division before being quietly released to the private security market, Amytal-X produces soldiers who can walk into catastrophic situations without hesitation.
effects: Complete suppression of fear, panic, and anxiety responses
Steady heart rate and clear cognition under fire
Preserved tactical judgment — unlike berserker compounds
Reduction of post-traumatic stress response formation
side_effects: Suppression of fear extends to suppression of survival instincts — users may fail to flee situations they should flee
Emotional blunting extending beyond fear to include empathy and social cognition
Difficulty forming emotional memories during duration — events feel distant and unreal
Rebound anxiety after drug clears, sometimes severe
Long-term use associated with acquired emotional blunting that does not fully resolve
Rare cases of persistent anhedonia in chronic users
cultural_context: Amytal-X is a drug for professionals — corporate security, high-end mercs, anyone who needs to be completely functional under conditions that would break an ordinary person. On the Tier 4-5 level, there's a quiet epidemic of off-label use: executives take it before hostile boardroom presentations, Spire security consultants take it before negotiations in dangerous districts. The drug's emotional blunting side effect has created a cohort of chronic users who describe themselves as 'just more efficient' and struggle to understand why their personal relationships have collapsed.
story_hooks: A Lazarus security operative who has been on Amytal-X for two years is assigned to protect a target she's been contracted to eventually betray — and she can no longer access the moral discomfort that would normally make this complicated.

Stolen Amytal-X tablets are appearing in the Gray Zone at prices Tier 1 residents can afford — someone is subsidizing the distribution, and the social effects in a community that runs on fear-based social control are already becoming visible.
A runner realizes mid-op that they took a tablet from a bottle that was swapped out — they feel nothing, including fear of the thing that is currently very wrong about this job.
